statements.label: supported
statements.text: Over 80% of broadly expressed vertebrate gene families with multiple whole-genome-duplication paralogues contain members that narrowed their ancestral expression.
statements.evidence: over 80% of broadly expressed gene families with multiple paralogues derived from whole-genome duplications have members that restricted their ancestral expression, and underwent specialization rather than subfunctionalization
statements.note: The abstract reports that over 80% of these vertebrate gene families have members that restricted their ancestral expression.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Paralogues that specialized after the vertebrate whole-genome duplications were linked to the origin of the neural crest.
statements.evidence: These data pave the way for a better understanding of the regulatory principles that underlie key vertebrate innovations.
statements.note: The abstract only says the data pave the way for understanding vertebrate innovations; it names no innovation and ties no paralogue to the neural crest.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Vertebrate paralogues that narrowed their expression ended up with regulatory landscapes of increased complexity.
statements.evidence: Counter-intuitively, paralogues that restricted their expression increased the complexity of their regulatory landscapes.
statements.note: The abstract states that paralogues which restricted their expression increased the complexity of their regulatory landscapes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Conservation of gene expression and cis-regulatory logic between amphioxus and vertebrates peaked during a mid-embryonic phylotypic period.
statements.evidence: a high conservation of gene expression and its cis-regulatory logic between amphioxus and vertebrates that occurs maximally at an earlier mid-embryonic phylotypic period
statements.note: The abstract reports high conservation of expression and cis-regulatory logic that occurs maximally at a mid-embryonic phylotypic period.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: For three of the ten phyla, the mid-developmental transition overlapped a previously defined phylotypic period.
statements.evidence: This mid-developmental transition overlaps with the phylotypic period that has been defined previously for three of the ten phyla
statements.note: The abstract states that the mid-developmental transition overlaps the phylotypic period previously defined for three of the ten phyla.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Gene expression was conserved during both the early and the late developmental phases in each of the ten species.
statements.evidence: We find that in all ten species, development comprises the coupling of early and late phases of conserved gene expression.
statements.note: The abstract reports that in all ten species development couples early and late phases of conserved gene expression.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Species with indirect development through a larval stage had a longer mid-developmental transition than direct developers.
statements.evidence: Here we compare the developmental transcriptomes of ten species, each annotated to a different phylum, with a wide range of life histories and embryonic forms.
statements.note: The abstract notes the species differ in life history but never compares the length of the mid-developmental transition between direct and indirect developers.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The mid-developmental transition linking the two phases used signalling pathways and transcription factors that differed from one species to another.
statements.evidence: These phases are linked by a divergent 'mid-developmental transition' that uses species-specific suites of signalling pathways and transcription factors.
statements.note: The abstract describes the linking transition as divergent and using species-specific suites of signalling pathways and transcription factors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Amphioxus and vertebrate karyotypes trace back to 17 ancestral chordate linkage groups through fusion, rearrangement and duplication.
statements.evidence: We show how the karyotypes of amphioxus and diverse vertebrates are derived from 17 ancestral chordate linkage groups (and 19 ancestral bilaterian groups) by fusion, rearrangement and duplication.
statements.note: The abstract derives amphioxus and vertebrate karyotypes from 17 ancestral chordate linkage groups by fusion, rearrangement and duplication.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The duplication found only in jawed vertebrates came later than the one all living vertebrates share, occurring in the mid-late Ordovician by allotetraploidization.
statements.evidence: the second duplication is found only in jawed vertebrates and occurred in the mid-late Ordovician by allotetraploidization
statements.note: The abstract calls the jawed-vertebrate event the second duplication and places it in the mid-late Ordovician, by allotetraploidization.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The duplication shared by all living vertebrates happened in the mid/late Cambrian through autotetraploidization, a direct doubling of the genome.
statements.evidence: All extant vertebrates share the first duplication, which occurred in the mid/late Cambrian by autotetraploidization (that is, direct genome doubling).
statements.note: The abstract states that the first duplication, shared by all extant vertebrates, occurred in the mid/late Cambrian by direct genome doubling.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Each of the two vertebrate genome duplications coincided with a mass extinction recorded in the fossil record.
statements.evidence: This complex genomic history parallels the diversification of vertebrate lineages in the fossil record.
statements.note: The abstract links the genomic history only to the diversification of vertebrate lineages in the fossil record, not to any mass extinction.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The scallop genome contains a lower proportion of transposable elements than other sequenced mollusc genomes.
statements.evidence: a bivalve mollusc that has a slow-evolving genome with many ancestral features
statements.note: The abstract calls the scallop genome slow-evolving with many ancestral features but reports nothing about its transposable element content.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transcriptomes of scallop mantle eyes revealed unexpectedly diverse phototransduction cascades and a Pax2/5/8-dependent pathway for non-cephalic eyes.
statements.evidence: Transcriptome analysis of scallop mantle eyes finds unexpected diversity in phototransduction cascades and a potentially ancient Pax2/5/8-dependent pathway for noncephalic eyes.
statements.note: The abstract reports unexpected phototransduction diversity and a Pax2/5/8-dependent pathway for noncephalic eyes in the mantle-eye transcriptomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The 19 scallop chromosomes correspond to the 17 presumed ancestral bilaterian linkage groups with a higher level of conservation than seen before.
statements.evidence: Chromosome-based macrosynteny analysis reveals a striking correspondence between the 19 scallop chromosomes and the 17 presumed ancestral bilaterian linkage groups at a level of conservation previously unseen
statements.note: The abstract describes the correspondence between 19 scallop chromosomes and 17 ancestral linkage groups as a level of conservation previously unseen.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Expression of scallop Hox genes follows temporal co-linearity organized by subclusters, a previously undescribed mode.
statements.evidence: Scallop Hox gene expression follows a new mode of subcluster temporal co-linearity
statements.note: The abstract states that scallop Hox expression follows a new mode of subcluster temporal co-linearity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genes kept in duplicate after the teleost-specific genome duplication 320 million years ago were no likelier to remain duplicated after the Ss4R.
statements.evidence: genes that were retained as duplicates after the teleost-specific whole-genome duplication 320 million years ago were not more likely to be retained after the Ss4R
statements.note: The abstract reports that duplicates retained from the 320-million-year-old teleost duplication were not more likely to be retained after the Ss4R.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Post-Ss4R rediploidization in Atlantic salmon depended on large genomic reorganizations that coincided with bursts of transposon-mediated repeat proliferation.
statements.evidence: large genomic reorganizations, coinciding with bursts of transposon-mediated repeat expansions, were crucial for the post-Ss4R rediploidization process
statements.note: The abstract states that large genomic reorganizations, coinciding with bursts of transposon-mediated repeat expansions, were crucial for post-Ss4R rediploidization.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The new Atlantic salmon assembly is more contiguous than previously published salmonid genome assemblies.
statements.evidence: the Atlantic salmon assembly can serve as a reference sequence for the study of other salmonids
statements.note: The abstract calls the assembly high-quality and a reference for other salmonids but never compares its contiguity with other salmonid assemblies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with orthologues in a pre-Ss4R outgroup, salmon duplicate-gene expression across tissues pointed to neofunctionalization far more often than subfunctionalization.
statements.evidence: Comparisons of duplicate gene expression patterns across a wide range of tissues with orthologous genes from a pre-Ss4R outgroup unexpectedly demonstrate far more instances of neofunctionalization than subfunctionalization.
statements.note: The abstract reports far more instances of neofunctionalization than subfunctionalization in comparisons with a pre-Ss4R outgroup.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Although organoids differed metabolically, they retained gene regulatory networks linked to primary cell types and developmental processes.
statements.evidence: Despite metabolic differences, organoid models preserve gene regulatory networks related to primary cell types and developmental processes.
statements.note: The abstract states that organoid models preserve gene regulatory networks for primary cell types and developmental processes despite metabolic differences.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Human radial glia showed elevated PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway activation that depended on INSR and ITGB8, two receptors upregulated specifically in humans.
statements.evidence: We observed increased activation of this pathway in human radial glia, dependent on two receptors upregulated specifically in human: INSR and ITGB8.
statements.note: The abstract reports increased PI3K-AKT-mTOR activation in human radial glia, dependent on the human-specifically upregulated receptors INSR and ITGB8.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Recent gene duplications were overrepresented among 261 genes that human samples expressed differently from both chimpanzee organoids and macaque cortex.
statements.evidence: We further identified 261 differentially expressed genes in human compared to both chimpanzee organoids and macaque cortex, enriched for recent gene duplications
statements.note: The abstract reports 261 genes differentially expressed in human versus both chimpanzee organoids and macaque cortex, enriched for recent gene duplications.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Chimpanzee cerebral organoids grew to a smaller size than human cerebral organoids.
statements.evidence: However, chimpanzee tissue is inaccessible during neocortical neurogenesis when differences in brain size first appear.
statements.note: The abstract mentions brain-size differences only as background and reports no measurement of organoid size.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Four in five of the 101 million significantly constrained single bases lie outside protein-coding exons, and half lack any ENCODE functional annotation.
statements.evidence: Of 101 million significantly constrained single bases, 80% are outside protein-coding exons and half have no functional annotations in the Encyclopedia of DNA Elements (ENCODE) resource.
statements.note: The abstract reports that 80% of the 101 million constrained single bases are outside protein-coding exons and half have no ENCODE annotation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The 4552 ultraconserved elements are concentrated near genes that control embryonic development.
statements.evidence: 4552 ultraconserved elements are nearly perfectly conserved
statements.note: The abstract gives only the number of ultraconserved elements and says nothing about which genes they lie near.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Exceptional mammalian traits, hibernation among them, were linked to changes in genes and regulatory elements.
statements.evidence: Changes in genes and regulatory elements are associated with exceptional mammalian traits, such as hibernation
statements.note: The abstract states that changes in genes and regulatory elements are associated with exceptional mammalian traits such as hibernation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: No less than 332 million bases, about 10.7% of the human genome, are more conserved across species than neutrally evolving repeats.
statements.evidence: At least 332 million bases (~10.7%) in the human genome are unusually conserved across species (evolutionarily constrained) relative to neutrally evolving repeats
statements.note: The abstract reports that at least 332 million human bases (~10.7%) are unusually conserved across species relative to neutrally evolving repeats.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The chromatin accessibility landscape is established faster in mouse early embryos than in human early embryos.
statements.evidence: we report that the chromatin accessibility landscape is gradually established during human early embryogenesis
statements.note: The abstract describes gradual establishment of accessibility in human embryos only; its human-mouse comparisons concern OCT4 motifs and ZGA, not the pace of accessibility.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The active human transposons SVA and HERV-K carry DHSs and are strongly expressed in early embryos but not in differentiated tissues.
statements.evidence: human active transposons SVA and HERV-K harbor DHSs and are highly expressed in early embryos, but not in differentiated tissues
statements.note: The abstract reports that SVA and HERV-K harbor DHSs and are highly expressed in early embryos but not in differentiated tissues.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Younger genes usually establish promoter DHSs and switch on expression at later embryonic stages than older genes.
statements.evidence: younger genes tend to establish promoter DHSs and are expressed at later embryonic stages, while older genes exhibit these features at earlier stages
statements.note: The abstract states that younger genes tend to establish promoter DHSs and be expressed at later stages, older genes at earlier stages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: DNase I hypersensitive sites with OCT4 binding motifs were overrepresented at zygotic genome activation in human embryos, a pattern absent in mice.
statements.evidence: the DHSs with OCT4 binding motifs are enriched at the timing of zygotic genome activation (ZGA) in humans, but not in mice
statements.note: The abstract reports that DHSs with OCT4 motifs are enriched at the timing of ZGA in humans but not in mice.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Insects with complete metamorphosis carry more novel gene families than insects with incomplete metamorphosis.
statements.evidence: examples of gene family and protein domain evolution coincident with the appearance of notable phenotypic and physiological adaptations such as flight, metamorphosis, sociality, and chemoperception
statements.note: The abstract ties gene family evolution to metamorphosis in general but does not compare novel gene family counts between complete and incomplete metamorphosis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Many novel gene families originated early in arthropod evolution, and others arose as insects diversified into modern orders.
statements.evidence: We identify many novel gene families that arose early in the evolution of arthropods and during the diversification of insects into modern orders.
statements.note: The abstract reports many novel gene families arising early in arthropod evolution and during the diversification of insects into modern orders.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 76 genomes from 21 orders spanning more than 500 million years of arthropod evolution, the study charted changes in gene and protein-domain content.
statements.evidence: Using 76 whole genome sequences representing 21 orders spanning more than 500 million years of arthropod evolution, we document changes in gene and protein domain content
statements.note: The abstract documents gene and protein domain content changes across 76 genomes from 21 orders spanning more than 500 million years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Patterns of DNA methylation varied across arthropods to an unexpected degree.
statements.evidence: We reveal unexpected variation in patterns of DNA methylation across arthropods
statements.note: The abstract reports unexpected variation in DNA methylation patterns across arthropods.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Together, the A. shenzhenica draft genome, transcriptomes from three subfamilies and third-generation genomes of two Epidendroideae species covered all five orchid subfamilies.
statements.evidence: In addition, we present transcriptome data for representatives of Vanilloideae, Cypripedioideae and Orchidoideae, and novel third-generation genome data for two species of Epidendroideae, covering all five orchid subfamilies.
statements.note: The abstract states that its transcriptome and third-generation genome data, alongside the A. shenzhenica genome, cover all five orchid subfamilies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Orchid evolution involved new gene families, expansions as well as contractions of existing families, and changes within MADS-box gene classes.
statements.evidence: We identify new gene families, gene family expansions and contractions, and changes within MADS-box gene classes, which control a diverse suite of developmental processes, during orchid evolution.
statements.note: The abstract reports new gene families, gene family expansions and contractions, and MADS-box class changes during orchid evolution.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Epiphytic orchids carry larger genomes than terrestrial orchids.
statements.evidence: This study sheds new light on the genetic mechanisms underpinning key orchid innovations, including the development of the labellum and gynostemium, pollinia, and seeds without endosperm, as well as the evolution of epiphytism
statements.note: The abstract mentions the evolution of epiphytism but compares no genome sizes between epiphytic and terrestrial orchids.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A whole-genome duplication seen in A. shenzhenica is common to all orchids and occurred a short time earlier than the orchids diverged.
statements.evidence: A. shenzhenica shows clear evidence of a whole-genome duplication, which is shared by all orchids and occurred shortly before their divergence.
statements.note: The abstract states that the whole-genome duplication in A. shenzhenica is shared by all orchids and occurred shortly before their divergence.
